record.paper_title: Some open problems in mathematical relativity
record.original_question: Does an apparent horizon persist under Einstein evolution of the initial data set, or can one exhibit an explicit counterexample to persistence?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $(M, g, K)$ be a smooth initial data set for the vacuum Einstein equations, where $M$ is a 3-manifold, $g$ is a Riemannian metric on $M$, and $K$ is a symmetric (0,2)-tensor on $M$ satisfying the vacuum constraint equations. Suppose $\Sigma \subset M$ is a smooth closed two-sided surface that is an apparent horizon at time $t=0$, that is, $\Sigma$ is (a connected component of the boundary of) the trapped region in $(M,g,K)$, equivalently a marginally outer trapped surface (MOTS) for which the outgoing null expansion $\theta_+ = H_\Sigma + \mathrm{tr}_\Sigma K$ vanishes. Let $(\mathcal{M}, \mathbf{g})$ denote the maximal globally hyperbolic vacuum development of $(M, g, K)$, and consider any smooth foliation of a neighborhood of $M$ in $\mathcal{M}$ by spacelike Cauchy hypersurfaces $M_t$ with $M_0 = M$.

Question: Must there exist, for every such foliation (or for some natural foliation) and for every sufficiently small $t > 0$, an apparent horizon $\Sigma_t \subset M_t$ that depends continuously on $t$ with $\Sigma_0 = \Sigma$? In other words, does an apparent horizon necessarily persist under Einstein evolution of the initial data, or can one exhibit an explicit vacuum initial data set with an apparent horizon whose Einstein evolution contains a Cauchy slice arbitrarily close to the initial slice on which no apparent horizon homologous to $\Sigma$ exists?
artifact.status_search_result: Searches did not return a definitive resolution of the persistence-of-apparent-horizons question. Related work exists on dynamical formation of MOTS and on numerical horizon-finding, and constructions are known of initial data without MOTS whose future development contains a trapped region, but no clear theorem or counterexample establishing or refuting general persistence under Einstein evolution was found. The status appears to remain unresolved.

status_evidence.title: Construction of Cauchy data for the dynamical formation of apparent horizons and the Penrose Inequality
status_evidence.snippet: Smooth asymptotically flat Cauchy initial data without MOTS whose future evolution contains a trapped region bounded by an apparent horizon.
status_evidence.claim: Related work addresses formation (rather than persistence) of apparent horizons in Einstein evolution.

status_evidence.title: Revisiting the apparent horizon finding problem with multigrid methods
status_evidence.snippet: Apparent horizons can be defined locally in time, contrasting with the teleological event horizon.
status_evidence.claim: Apparent horizons are slicing-dependent objects, which is at the heart of the persistence question.
